stories.headline: Google Maps now shows 'Lake America' in U.S., not 'Lake Ontario'
stories.deck: Canadians will see 'Lake Ontario' and those outside U.S. and Canada will see both names, Google says, days after Donald Trump signed an order renaming the water body
stories.bodyText:
Google Maps has changed the name of “Lake Ontario” to “Lake America” for U.S. users to reflect President Donald Trump’s executive order renaming the lake, according to a Google statement.
Mr. Trump announced on Thursday (August 27, 2026) that he was changing the name of the smallest of the five Great Lakes, part of an escalating trade feud with Canada that has prompted the two countries to impose reciprocal tariffs on billions of dollars in goods.
The President’s order affects the U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS), which sets the standards for official U.S. maps. It does not have any impact on Canadian naming conventions or how the rest of the world refers to the lake.
“Since we update Google Maps to reflect name changes in official government sources, which is GNIS for the U.S., people using Maps in the U.S. will see ‘Lake America,’ those in Canada will continue to see ‘Lake Ontario,’ and those outside of the U.S. and Canada will see both names,” Google said in a blog post issued on Saturday.
The White House, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s office and Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s office did not immediately comment on Google’s decision on Sunday.
Google Maps made a similar change to the Gulf of Mexico last year, labelling it the “Gulf of America” following Trump’s executive order on his first day in office renaming the body of water.
Mr. Carney immediately rejected the lake’s name change on Thursday. Democratic Governor Kathy Hochul of New York, which shares a long border with Canada, declared that “New York won’t be calling it that,” while Phil Scott, the Republican governor of neighboring Vermont, called Mr. Trump’s decision “petty and disappointing” on social media.
In Ontario, Mr. Ford on Saturday unveiled a large lakeside sign that reads, “Lake Ontario: Now and Always,” in both English and French.
“President Trump can call it whatever he wants, but I can tell you, the rest of the world will always call it Lake Ontario,” Mr. Ford said.
On Sunday evening, an Ontario minister, Stephen Crawford, said the province was reviewing its websites after Lake America appeared on sites like the Liquor Control Board of Ontario. The LCBO, a major global buyer, is not stocking U.S. alcohol due to the trade war.
“Some Ontario government agency websites pull map data directly from Google Maps,” Mr. Crawford said on the social media site X. “Following recent changes by Google, we’re actively reviewing our websites to make sure they all identify Lake Ontario by its correct name: Lake Ontario”.

stories.headline: Pakistan’s Dar, Munir arrive in Turkiye ahead of first Makkah defence pact meeting
stories.deck: Under the agreement, an attack against one of the countries will be treated as an attack against all of them, amid increasing security concerns in the wake of escalating tensions in West Asia
stories.bodyText:
Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Asim Munir on Sunday (August 30, 2026) reached Turkiye for a trilateral defence pact meeting, which also includes Saudi Arabia.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the trilateral defence agreement, known as the 'Makkah Joint Defence Agreement', on August 7.
Under the agreement, an attack against one of the countries will be treated as an attack against all of them, amid increasing security concerns in the wake of escalating tensions in West Asia.
The Pakistan Foreign Office in a statement said Dar, who is also the foreign minister, had landed in Istanbul for “official engagements”.
Separately, the army said in a statement that Field Marshal Munir also arrived in Türkiye on an “official visit”.
The details of their engagements have not been shared officially.
However, the Turkish Foreign Ministry confirmed that the first meeting of the “Strategic Political and Defence Committee” established under the defence pact will be held in Istanbul on Monday.
Turkiye said its Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Defence Minister Yasar Guler and Chief of Turkish General Staff Gen Selcuk Bayraktaroglu will participate in the meeting.
The agenda of the first meeting under the defence agreement is not known, but it is believed that the regional situation with respect to the Iran war would be discussed.
Separately, Turkiye’s Fidan also invited Dar to the Regional-4 meeting in Istanbul, which includes the three countries part of the defence pact, along with Egypt.
The R-4 group, which has been focused on regional security, emerged in March amid efforts for mediation between the US and Iran.
The last R-4 meeting was held on August 5 in Jordan’s capital Amman, where the ministers “reaffirmed the importance of continued consultation and close coordination among the four countries in advancing regional stability”, according to the Foreign Office.
Pakistan has sought to play a mediatory role between the U.S. and Iran.
Mr. Dar travelled to Turkiye from London where he “concluded a successful official visit to the UK”, according to the Foreign Office.

stories.headline: Explained: Why ICC stripped Sri Lanka of 2027 Women’s CT hosting rights
stories.deck: The ICC has removed Sri Lanka’s hosting rights for the inaugural Women’s Champions Trophy in 2027 over government interference in Sri Lanka Cricket. The tournament will be moved elsewhere, with the venue yet to be decided. Sri Lanka could also miss out as hosts because they are ranked sixth. The ICC wants SLC to return to an elected administration.
stories.bodyText:
The International Cricket Council (ICC) has removed Sri Lanka’s hosting rights for the first-ever Women’s Champions Trophy, scheduled for 2027, because of concerns over government involvement in the running of Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC).
The tournament was expected to feature six teams, including the host nation, but the change could also affect Sri Lanka’s place in the competition.
Sri Lanka had been selected to host the inaugural women’s Champions Trophy, but the ICC is now expected to move the event to another country. The new venue has not yet been decided and could be discussed at the ICC’s next board meeting.
Prakash Shaffter, Secretary of the SLC Transformation Committee, confirmed the change, saying, “Yes, it has been moved out of Sri Lanka. It will be played at another venue, but as of now, I am not sure where it will be played.”
The decision could also cause a financial setback for Sri Lanka Cricket. More importantly, Sri Lanka’s women’s team could lose its automatic place in the tournament. The event was planned to include the top five ranked teams along with the host country. Sri Lanka are currently ranked sixth.
ICC wants elected cricket administration
Sri Lanka Cricket is currently being managed by a government-appointed Transformation Committee. 
The committee was created to oversee reforms, including changes to the board’s constitution and governance system.
However, the ICC has not recognised the politically appointed interim administration. “The ICC does not recognise politically appointed interim administrations and has refused to allow SLC representatives to attend ICC Board meetings since the Transformation Committee took over,” the report said.
In July, the ICC said, “The ICC Board received an update on Sri Lanka Cricket and noted progress towards a revised Constitution.”
“It reiterated the need for elections to be held as soon as possible and agreed that Sri Lanka Cricket would continue to be unable to be represented at ICC Board meetings for the time being.”
The proposed constitutional changes still need to complete the legal process before reaching Parliament, meaning Sri Lanka’s return to an elected administration could take time.
The ICC had taken similar action in 2023, when Sri Lanka lost the hosting rights for the 2024 U-19 World Cup after its elected cricket administration was dissolved and replaced with an interim committee.

stories.headline: Bizarre! Cricket team loses match due to broken print - here's how
stories.deck: Ballyspallen were forced to concede their Northern Ireland cricket match against Eglinton after a broken printer prevented officials from producing a required Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) sheet following rain. Eglinton had scored 159, while Ballyspallen were 19-0 when play stopped. League rules require the home side to concede if the DLS sheet cannot be provided to teams and umpires.
stories.bodyText:
A broken printer has resulted in a cricket team conceding a match in Northern Ireland, turning what looked like a normal rain interruption into a highly unusual defeat.
Ballyspallen were playing at home against Eglinton in the North West Cricket Union Premier League on Saturday. Eglinton had been bowled out for 159 runs in 48.1 overs and Ballyspallen had started their chase. The hosts had scored 19 runs after two overs when rain stopped play.
Because of the weather, the number of overs in the match was expected to be reduced. Officials therefore needed to use the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method, which is used in cricket to work out a revised target when rain interrupts a limited-overs match.
However, the required DLS sheet could not be produced because Ballyspallen's printer was not working. Without the document, officials could not continue the match under the competition's rules.
Eglinton were consequently awarded the victory, even though not another ball was bowled after the rain delay. The unusual decision was based on the North West Cricket Union's regulations, which specifically cover situations where a DLS calculation cannot be provided.
Home team penalised under strict regulations
According to the rules, the team hosting the match must immediately concede if a DLS sheet cannot be produced for both teams and the umpires.
The regulations also clearly state that the home club should have "a computer loaded with the necessary software, a compatible and operational printer with a sufficient supply of paper and ink, and a proficient operator".
The NWCU further says this equipment must be "operational" before the match starts. Ballyspallen's failure to meet that requirement therefore proved costly.
The technical problem denied Ballyspallen the opportunity to continue their chase and potentially secure their fifth Premier League victory. Instead, Eglinton took the points without having to bowl another delivery, while Ballyspallen remain at the bottom of the league table.

stories.headline: Oil jumps more than 2% after US attack on Iran's Larak island
stories.bodyText: Singapore: Oil prices jumped more than 2% on Monday, with Brent back above $90 a barrel, after US forces struck two Iranian launchers on Iran's Larak island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, the first known American strikes on the Gulf nation since late July.Brent crude futures climbed $2.22, or 2.52%, to $90.32 a barrel by 2202 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $85.41 a barrel, up $2.01, or 2.41%.

briefs.headline: U.S. forces strike Iranian rocket launchers on the Strait of Hormuz in first military action in weeks
briefs.deck: A U.S. officials says that U.S. forces have struck Iranian rocket launchers on the Strait of Hormuz in the first military action in a month
briefs.bodyText:
U.S. forces have struck Iranian rocket launchers on the Strait of Hormuz in the first military action in a month, a U.S. official said Sunday.
Semiofficial news outlets in Iran reported sounds of explosions near Larak island on the strait.
Forces with the Revolutionary Guard Corps were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the strait, according to the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to detail sensitive military movements.
The U.S. military last week completed clearing sea mines from the strait’s international shipping routes.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards vow response to U.S. attack on Larak island
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said a U.S. attack on Larak Island killed and wounded several Iranian fighters and civilians, and vowed to respond and punish those responsible, state broadcaster IRIB reported.
The Guards did not provide a precise casualty toll.
(With inputs from AP and Reuters)

briefs.headline: Nepal-China flash flood disaster exposes fragility of Hindu Kush Himalayas: U.N. climate chief
briefs.deck: The death toll from flash floods in Nepal rose to 788 with more bodies being recovered, even as more than 2,500 people are still missing
briefs.bodyText:
The glacial collapse and flash flood near the Nepal-China border are a devastating reminder of how fragile mountain environments can be, particularly in the Hindu Kush Himalayas, UN climate chief Simon Stiell said on Sunday (August 30, 2026).
He said scientists and local communities have been warning for years that the Hindu Kush Himalayas are at huge risk owing to climate change.
"We also know a warming climate, driven by humanity burning colossal amounts of coal, oil and gas, is making tragedies like this one, and so many others around the world, much more likely, frequent and severe, with vulnerable communities often hardest hit," said Mr. Stiell, the executive secretary of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).
"But the solutions to global heating are equally clear — especially a faster global shift from fossil fuels to renewables and more investment in climate resilience," he added.
On Sunday (August 30), the death toll from flash floods in Nepal rose to 788 with more bodies being recovered, even as more than 2,500 people are still missing. Rescuers raced against time to search for those missing and rescue those stranded on the fifth day since the disaster.
An ice-rock avalanche following a glacial collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border sent a torrent of water, mud and debris downstream, wiping out towns and villages, damaging crucial infrastructure and washing away hydropower stations through northern and central Nepal on August 26.
Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) said the death toll has surged to 788.
The Bhotekoshi river, which flows south from the Himalayan border region, carried the floodwaters downstream, creating havoc on August 26.
On Saturday, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said that more than 275 Indians and 128 persons of Indian origin remained missing or non-contactable in Nepal. On Sunday, the MEA on its X handle shared a list of 149 people who were rescued.

briefs.headline: IPL media rights: Does the BCCI have a Plan B?
briefs.deck: With JioStar the only serious bidder in sight, Indian cricket risks leaving value on the table
briefs.bodyText:
The Indian cricket board's reluctance to seek better price discovery ahead of the upcoming IPL and home bilateral media rights tender is weighing heavily on the industry.
With about six months to go before the final IPL edition of the 2023-27 rights cycle begins, there is growing concern among cricket's biggest stakeholders that the absence of a credible bidder other than JioStar will prevent an accurate assessment of the property's value, and, in turn, deny the market the competitive tension that has driven IPL rights upwards for a decade.
That sentiment was echoed by none other than Uday Shankar, the media entrepreneur who serves as vice-chairman of JioStar, at the recent ET World Leaders Forum.
"Ten years ago, you would have multiple and serious media companies (around four) competing for major sports rights. You'd have four or more companies genuinely fighting for properties. Today, increasingly, it feels as if we are the only ones standing. And that's not healthy," Shankar said.
"The fundamental issue is that the cost of the rights has risen dramatically. But the ability to monetise those rights hasn't necessarily risen at the same rate. The value of sports is enormous, but the rights holder, broadcaster and platform all need to participate in a sustainable ecosystem," he added.
The worrying part of this narrative is the absence of a Plan B for Indian cricket. That JioStar will bid healthily for the IPL is a given: its subscription numbers are heavily leveraged against cricket consumption. 
What is baffling is the BCCI's inability to bring more participants to the table.
Players such as YouTube and Netflix have been engaging aggressively with sport in the West. YouTube's move into rights aggregation and bundling has, in fact, become an industry trend of its own.
YouTube increasingly treats sport not as a series of standalone rights acquisitions but as the anchor of a broader pay-TV and subscription ecosystem. Its seven-year deal for exclusive US distribution of NFL Sunday Ticket — worth a reported $2 billion a season — works both as a value-add for YouTube TV subscribers and as a standalone product sold through YouTube channels.
Average revenue per user in the West bears little resemblance to what the subcontinent generates, which complicates the assumption that volume alone wins the argument. Even so, Indian cricket remains the only market in this part of the world worth a player like YouTube testing the waters in.
More recently, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos told The Economic Times that the streaming giant was interested in live sport, including cricket, but had no intention of becoming a "conventional full-season sports broadcaster".
If so, a property like the IPL sits squarely in Netflix's territory. The storytelling potential of an India-first sports property speaks to a billion-plus domestic audience, a vast global diaspora, and to markets where cricket remains one of India's most effective exports and a quiet instrument of soft power.
"At some point, the economics have to make sense," Shankar says. For that to happen, the responsibility must lie with the federation itself to market what is, by any measure, a high-value product.
The IPL may be India's most prized prime-time asset. But to assume that a media player several time zones away is fully clued in to the India story, without hearing it first-hand from the people writing it, is optimistic at best.
Which is why it matters that the BCCI arrives at this tender with a genuine marketing strategy: one that puts the IPL in front of the dozens of media, technology and streaming platforms worldwide that could plausibly be interested.
JioStar is the BCCI's Plan A. The question is whether there is a Plan B, or a Plan C.

briefs.headline: FIR registered against Rahul Gandhi over Haldwani 'purification' remarks
briefs.bodyText: Haldwani: An FIR has been registered against Rahul Gandhi, following a complaint by a member of the Valmiki community in Haldwani alleging that the Congress leader gave a casteist spin to a religious ritual held at the venue of the AICC chief's programme, police said on Sunday..The FIR has been registered under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) concerning the promotion of enmity between groups and deliberate acts intended to outrage religious feelings. The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, has also been invoked, police said..Amit Kumar, a resident of Jawahar Nagar and a Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas member, claimed in the complaint filed at the Haldwani police station that he was present during the "ritual and cleanliness drive" and Gandhi's remarks made in Delhi at a press conference on August 29 hurt the sentiments of the community..KPSC 'rotting' under Congress govt, Rahul Gandhi should meet victims: H D Kumaraswamy.He accused Gandhi of portraying those associated with the ritual as practising "untouchability" and being "anti-Dalit"..In the complaint, Kumar claimed that he belongs to the Scheduled Caste community and that people from different sections of society, including Scheduled Castes, were involved in the ritual, which, according to him, had "no connection" with Congress president Mallkarjun Kharge's caste..A political row erupted after some individuals allegedly performed a 'purification yajna' at the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani on August 11, following a public meeting held there by Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge on August 8..While the Congress has termed the incident a reflection of the BJP's anti-Dalit mindset, the BJP defended the action, claiming that the venue was left littered after Kharge's rally and that slogans were raised which were inappropriate for a religious site..At a press conference in New Delhi on August 29, Gandhi criticised the incident and demanded registration of an FIR under the SC/ST Act against those responsible for the "purification"..Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra subsequently joined the demand for action, describing the incident as a reflection of a "reprehensible and shameful mindset" and alleging that it amounted to a violation of the SC/ST Act.

briefs.headline: Ahead of SCO, Uzbekistan joins India in condemning cross-border terrorism
briefs.deck: Uzbekistan and India have elevated their relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership. Both nations unequivocally condemned terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, in a joint statement. This marks a significant diplomatic alignment on regional security dynamics and counter-terrorism efforts. Leaders called for concerted actions against terrorist entities and disrupting financing…
briefs.bodyText:
As the two countries elevated their relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership, Uzbekistan joined India in unequivocally condemning, in a joint statement, terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, in all its forms and manifestations, reiterated a zero-tolerance approach to terrorism and rejected justification of terrorism on any ground whatsoever.
Even though the two countries share strong counter-terrorism cooperation, this formulation is significant as Uzbekistan has not used the specific phrase “cross-border terrorism” in past apex level joint statements, like those issued after summit meetings in 2015, 2018 and in 2020. As per sources, this reflects stronger diplomatic alignment on state-sponsored terrorism and regional security dynamics, especially in the context of the SCO summit Tuesday in which leaders will address issues like the need for stronger counter-terrorism measures and the Afghanistan situation.
“The leaders called for concerted actions against terrorist entities and for disrupting terrorism financing networks, safe havens and infrastructure. They stressed that those responsible for terrorism should be held accountable and their perpetrators, their backers, facilitators and affiliates should be brought to justice,” said the statement.
Share your thoughts in the comments
Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
The strongest wording so far had come in the 2020 joint statement, after a virtual summit, in which PM Narendra Modi and President Shavkat Mirziyoyev condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations and also underlined the need for every country to ensure that its territory is not used to launch terrorist attacks against other countries.
Read more: 
India, Uzbekistan target long-term uranium pact
The leaders stressed the importance of strengthening cooperation in law enforcement and intelligence-sharing, and combating violent extremism, illicit drug trafficking, organised crime and cyber threats. They also reaffirmed in the joint statement the importance of continued cooperation under the joint working group on counter-terrorism.
India and Uzbekistan, which shares a border with Afghanistan, have shared concerns about radicalisation and influx of militant groups. For India, it’s important to work with Uzbekistan and other countries in the region to prevent Afghanistan from turning into a haven for terrorist groups, particularly like the LeT and JeM based in Pakistan. Tashkent is also home to RATS, a permanent SCO body responsible for coordinating efforts by member-states against terrorism, extremism and separatism.

stories.headline: Islam is 'greater' than other religions: Karnataka higher education minister Basavaraj Rayareddi
stories.deck: Karnataka minister Basavaraj Rayareddi stated Islam is a great religion. His comments at a Muslim community event drew sharp criticism from the opposition. BJP leader R Ashoka demanded Rayareddi withdraw his statements and apologize. Ashoka also called for the minister's removal from the cabinet. The opposition accused the Congress government of an anti-Hindu mindset.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Karnataka higher education minister Basavaraj Rayareddi on Sunday said Islam is "greater" than other religions, news agency PTI reported.
He expressed his desire to visit Mecca, but said he cannot do so as a non-Muslim.
The minister made the remarks while speaking at a mass marriage programme for the Muslim community in Kuknoor in Koppal district.
According to PTI, Rayareddi said, "I would like to say that Islam is shreshta dharam (great religion) than other dharmas...."
He said there are misconceptions about the religion and added that he had tried to study the Quran, other religions and their history.
Later, describing Islam as highly disciplined, highly scientific and the most humane religion, he said, "Read it, understand, and don't become bigots, don't become casteists. There are good and bad people in all religions, but bad things are always highlighted... We should respect all religions, we should know good things in all religions as religions are for well being of mankind and we should try to do good."
"Islam is a good religion. I'm speaking here very happily. I'm thinking very much about going to Mecca, but I can't go there as one should convert to Islam (to go there). It's a tradition in that religion," he said.
"Islam is a good religion, there are good teachings in it, you should follow it, instead of just going to Masjid...," he added.
His remarks drew a sharp reaction from BJP leader R Ashoka, who said that by stating, in effect, that "Islam is greater than other religions," Rayareddi had portrayed Sanatana Dharma in an inferior light.
Ashoka, the leader of the opposition in the Assembly, demanded that Rayareddi withdraw his statements and apologise to all Hindus in the state.
He also said that if Rayareddi refused, chief minister DK Shivakumar should demonstrate his commitment by removing him from the Cabinet.
"CM Shivakumar, is there no end to the anti-Hindu mindset of your Congress government? You go around visiting temples and putting on a display of devotion before cameras, but why do you remain silent when ministers in your own Cabinet make derogatory statements about Sanatana Hindu Dharma and temples," he asked.
Ashoka further said, "... by stating, in effect, that Islam is greater than other religions, he has portrayed Sanatana Dharma in an inferior light."
Questioning whether this was the Congress party's idea of "equal respect for all religions", Ashoka asked, "Is this your vision of a garden of peace for all communities? Or are all your theatrics and pretence merely another mask worn to secure Hindu votes?
He said that if Rayareddi did not apologise or was not removed from the ministry, crores of Hindus in Karnataka would be left with one conclusion: "Your (CM) temple visits are not out of devotion. Your words are not out of respect for Hindu Dharma. Everything is merely for votes and for show."
He further accused the Congress of being "Anti-Hindu".
(With inputs from PTI)

stories.headline: Massive crowd walks through Bengaluru’s Lalbagh to oppose tunnel road
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A massive crowd, including senior citizens and children, walked through Lalbagh Sunday, opposing the proposed tunnel road and the recent amendment allowing up to 5% of park land to be diverted for other uses.
Led by environmentalist AN Yellappa Reddy, the walk was joined by all four Bengaluru MPs, Jayanagar MLA CK Ramamurthy, and actors Sudha Belawadi, Samyukta Hornad and Pranita Subhash. Members of pro-Kannada organisations, RWAs and other outfits joined the march.
CN Manjunath, Bangalore Rural MP, said: “The amendment is totally against the very purpose of Karnataka Parks (Preservation) Act. The governor should return the bill to the assembly. Bengaluru requires at least 30,000 acres of parks, but has only around 3,000 acres.”
Bangalore North MP Shobha Karandlaje said the city needed more lung spaces. “But this is a real estate govt which sees money when it sees vacant spaces. We are not anti-development, but don’t touch our parks and lakes. There’s no discussion on development. Wherever there is a money-making opportunity, the govt thinks about that,” she said.
Bangalore Central MP PC Mohan termed the amendment “draconian” and alleged that it had been passed without discussions. He claimed the amendment had been brought with the proposed tunnel project in mind. “This project has no scientific backing and is being done to benefit a company like Adani. Today it is 5%, it may increase to 25%,” he said.
Surya slams govt
Bangalore South MP 
Tejasvi Surya
 said police had issued him a notice and threatened to file FIRs for assembling in Lalbagh, allegedly on the instructions of chief minister DK Shivakumar. Calling the move “shameful”, Surya said: “If asking for the protection of Lalbagh is a crime, I am ready to commit this crime every single day.”
Surya put forward two demands — withdrawal of the amendment allowing up to 5% of park land to be used for infrastructure projects and dropping of the tunnel road project. He claimed 5,000-6,000 people had arrived in Lalbagh to oppose the tunnel road and protect the park.
“Development does not mean snatching five acres of Lalbagh or 3.5 acres of Hebbal Lake,” he said, alleging that engineers were also conducting soil testing at MN Krishna Rao Park. “If this continues, Bengaluru’s parks will be converted to real estate sites,” he said.
Songs, postcards and signatures
Citizens of all age groups marched from the West Gate to Lalbagh Rock, raising slogans against the amendment and the tunnel road project. Several participants lay on the rock and hugged it, signalling their commitment to protecting the landmark.
On the rock, Surya led participants in a mass singing of a popular Rajkumar song from ‘Gandhadagudi,’ the Kannada film known for its celebration of Karnataka’s natural wealth. Carnatic vocalist Spoorthi Rao led a rendition of Vande Mataram followed by a medley of film songs.
BV Sridhar Rao, a Lalbagh walker for over three decades, has been spearheading the campaign. “We received 3,000 postcards today, taking the total to over 4,000. We will intensify the campaign this week by reaching out to walkers entering through different gates, as people from different parts of the city use different gates,” he said.
“Several people were moved to tears today. A mother’s eyes welled up as she reminisced about her childhood days at Lalbagh and feared that her children may not have the same experience. Many other senior citizens, some over 80, became nostalgic, recalling their memories of Lalbagh from five decades or more,” Rao said. He added that the campaign would include collecting signatures written in blood in the coming weeks.
Participating in the march, activist Sajjan Raj Mehta said any damage to the city’s ecological heritage would be irreversible.
“Infrastructure can be redesigned. Roads can be realigned. Buildings can be relocated. But once a city’s ecological heritage is destroyed, it cannot simply be rebuilt,” he said.
General public and park users wrote postcards to the chief minister, urging him to drop the tunnel road project. Two large boards were also filled with signatures and messages from citizens calling for the protection of Lalbagh.

stories.headline: New traffic rules in Bengaluru: No entry for two-wheelers on KIA and e-city elevated corridors; more restrictions on five flyovers
stories.deck: The restrictions on the BGS Flyover, Peenya Elevated Corridor, Double-Decker Flyover and Kempe Gowda International Airport Road Elevated Corridor will come into effect from September 4.
stories.bodyText:
Come September, two-wheelers will be banned on two major elevated corridors — Airport Road (towards KIA) and Electronics City — in Bengaluru, a move aimed at reducing accidents and improving traffic movement. The Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) has also announced restrictions on the movement of certain other categories of vehicles on five flyovers in the city.
According to the BTP, the decision follows a review of accidents on certain flyovers, particularly those attributed to variations in vehicle speeds. The restrictions on the BGS Flyover, Peenya Elevated Corridor, Double-Decker Flyover and Kempe Gowda International Airport Road Elevated Corridor will come into effect from September 4. Those on the Electronics City Elevated Corridor will be implemented from September 11.
The BTP said it considered several factors, including road safety, the design and width of the flyovers, severity of accidents, congestion caused by vehicle breakdowns, congestion at entry and exit points, traffic management during emergencies, and the safety of two-wheeler riders.
A senior traffic police officer told The Hindu that the move had been under consideration for a long time, as the number of accidents on the stretches was growing.
“A comprehensive review of data was done before taking the decision. We will review the impact of these restrictions and make necessary adjustments in the future,” the officer said.
Another officer explained that the Electronics City flyover is currently managed by Bangalore Elevated Tollway Pvt. Ltd. (BETPL), and its term will end soon. “There are talks about handing over the flyover to the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), but it is likely that the period could be extended. Even then, we will discuss with BETPL and make changes,” the officer said.
The move is likely to draw commuter outrage, especially two-wheeler restrictions, as both flyovers are used by thousands of office-goers in the city. The BTP has urged the public to cooperate with the initiative, stating that the measures have been introduced in the interest of public safety and smoother traffic movement.

stories.headline: Bengaluru street vendor Ningamma finds mention in PM’s Mann Ki Baat
stories.bodyText:
T.S. Ningamma, a street vendor from Bengaluru, was mentioned by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the 137th episode of his monthly radio programme, Mann Ki Baat, for how support under the PM SVANidhi scheme helped her expand her small food business.
The Prime Minister said Ms. Ningamma and her husband had started a small business of selling idli, dosa and sambar. While the business began to do well, the couple needed additional funds to expand it. “Ms. Ningamma subsequently received financial support under the PM SVANidhi scheme. With the additional capital, she made improvements to the business, began purchasing ingredients in bulk and expanded her menu by adding new items,” Mr. Modi said, adding that these changes helped bring in more customers, increased her earnings and improved the family’s financial condition.
Mr. Modi added that because of the support she received, Ms. Ningamma was now able to provide education to her three children. “When a woman’s business grows, the future of the entire family moves forward,” he said, adding that such women also gain greater confidence. He cited Ms. Ningamma as a ‘living example’ of women empowerment.

briefs.headline: Dangerous high: Student peddling arrests soar sixfold in Karnataka
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Karnataka
 is seeing a striking shift in the nature of drug cases involving students. While arrests for consumption are steadily declining, the number of students being arrested for allegedly supplying and peddling narcotics has surged more than sixfold in just two years — signalling a worrying change in how young people are becoming entangled in drug trade.
As many as 228 students have been arrested across the state in 2026 so far for alleged drug supply and peddling, up from 36 in 2024 — a 533% rise. In contrast, arrests of students for narcotics consumption declined from 415 in 2024 to 297 in 2025 and 167 so far this year.
The figures, provided by home minister Priyank Kharge in the legislative assembly recently, point to a worrying shift: student involvement in narcotics cases is moving beyond consumption and into the supply chain.
The trend is heavily concentrated in Bengaluru, which accounts for 177 of the 228 students arrested statewide — nearly 78%. The city has recorded another 12 arrests for consumption, taking its total student drug-related arrests to 189.
This also puts the spotlight on educational institutions, particularly high schools and colleges. In March, Bengaluru police screened students at six institutions and two hostels in Vijayanagar subdivision. 
Of the 585 students tested, 31 returned positive for substance use and were offered counselling and medical support.
In June, govt launched ‘Operation RISE’ and ‘Beda Bro’ campaign, with over 8.3 lakh students participating in awareness activities. Chief minister DK Shivakumar said: “The longer you hide your children’s addiction, the more you destroy their future,” while Kharge urged students to “say no, even if friends insist.” The state has scaled up awareness programmes, reaching over 5.8 million students through 66,656 programmes since 2024.
On enforcement, Kharge said an ADGP has been given additional charge of the state-level Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF). A proposal to empower ANTF to register FIRs and investigate drug trafficking cases is also under consideration, he said.
Steps taken to control drugs
* Narcotics Coordination (NCORD) committees formed at state and district levels
* Monthly awareness programmes inside schools and colleges by police
* Zero-narcotics zones, where constant vigilance is maintained around schools, colleges, PG hostels, and malls by a special squad
* Operation RISE (Refuse, Inform, Support, Empower) and Beda Bro campaigns launched
* Anti-Narcotics Day celebrated on June 26 every year
* Special patrolling and surprise checks to prevent drug parties at resorts/farm houses
* Awareness on crackdowns publicised through social media
* Heads of schools and colleges directed to form anti-drug clubs/committees
* Arrested offenders’ profiles and details systematically uploaded on the National Integrated Database on Arrested Narco Offenders (NIDAAN) portal and police IT software
* Swift legal action and registration of cases against foreign nationals involved in NDPS crimes
Stakeholders speak
The increase in numbers is driven by organised networks of old-time peddlers who lure teenagers into drug peddling on the promise of easy money. Teens active on social media and at parties also find it easier to build and expand these networks. The average age is below 18, with students typically peddling ganja and tablets because they are easily affordable. Parents, guardians and educational institutions must keep a close watch. If a child is found using or peddling drugs, they should be treated as a victim, not a wrongdoer. Family support, regular communication and counselling can help them break away from these networks. 
— Raja Imam Kasim P, DCP (crime)
Exposure to drugs is happening much earlier, mostly between ages 14 and 17. Many seek treatment only after something serious happens, often 3-4 years into substance use. Cannabis is highly prevalent, while access to drugs and information about them has increased. With the brain still developing, children are particularly vulnerable to peer and social media influence, affecting their education and mental health. Parents should watch for changes in sleep, appetite, academic performance, spending habits and social circles, as well as withdrawal from family. Open, non-judgmental conversations are crucial. 
— Mohith Rahul L, clinical psychologist at Cadabams Hospitals
Awareness is key. Colleges must have anti-drug squads comprising parents, students, staff and wardens, and must conduct awareness programmes every three months. We’ve also started wellness clinics and trained master trainers in yoga and meditation. More initiatives, including social warrior teams, are under way. — 
Bhavan BC, vice-chancellor, Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences

briefs.headline: More than just a date: Singles swap swipes for real conversations in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
On a rainy evening in Bengaluru, singles stepped out of their comfort zones to meet new people and forge fresh connections at a Speed Dating event hosted by Bangalore Times Life.Styled Club. The night was filled with games, playful dares and relaxed conversation, giving attendees a chance to set their phones aside and connect face to face.
Breaking the ice, one dare at a time The idea behind Speed Dating was to let participants meet several people in a relaxed setting, get a sense of each other’s personalities and move beyond the usual experience of dating apps. After brief introductions, participants were encouraged to interact through games and dares, making it easier to strike up conversations with strangers. The activities helped break the initial awkwardness, with participants laughing, taking on challenges and getting to know one another. What started with a little nervousness soon turned into lively conversations.
Content creator Sim Pereira believes such events are a good way to meet people outside one’s usual circle. “For someone who has moved to Bengaluru recently, these kinds of events are great because they put you on the spot to step out of your comfort zone. 
Everyone here has come with an open mind, so it makes it easier for people to get along,” she says.
She also feels such events can help people who may otherwise feel lonely in a new city. “It’s an excellent way to network, get to know people, especially in a place like Bengaluru, where it can be very easy to feel lonely. Even if you just want to make friends, it’s amazing,” she adds.
New city, new connections For Swarna, a financial consultant, the evening was a refreshing change from the usual ways of meeting people. “This event helped me step out of my comfort zone. The games and activities were easy, and conversations with strangers flowed very naturally and comfortably,” she says. Having attended similar social events in Pune, Swarna says this was her first such experience in Bengaluru. “I see a lot of people who are new to Bengaluru and don’t know the city much. Such events help people socialise more easily,” she says.
Aryan, a young start-up founder, thinks such events are great for introverts. “For me, it was about overcoming nervousness and meeting new people. I’ve been to business summits before where I met a lot of people, but this was more casual and fun. The dares were also a great way of bringing out the best in us,” he says. He feels Bengaluru is the right city for such experiences. “Bengaluru is a happening place, and things should always be happening. This is something Bengaluru people need,” he adds.
For someone who has moved to Bengaluru recently, these kinds of events are great because they put you on the spot to step out of your comfort zone
Sim Pereira, content creator who joined the event
As the session progressed, the initial hesitation gave way to laughter, conversations and new introductions. Not everyone may have walked away with a date, but the evening offered something equally valuable: the chance to meet people beyond their usual circles, make new friends and discover connections without the pressure of a dating app.
For Sim, that is perhaps the biggest takeaway. “You tend to hang out with the same kind of people in your friend groups. But here, there is a really good mix. You meet people from different walks of life,” she says, adding that meeting people offline offers cues that online interactions often miss. “You can kind of sense who they are through body language. There are more cues for you to know who a person is.”
 What is Life.Styled Club
Life.Styled Club is a curated community for those who don’t just follow a lifestyle, but style life itself. The club brings people together through exclusive experiences designed to spark conversations and build new connections.

briefs.headline: More wards, same workforce: GBA, corporations struggle to deliver on the ground
briefs.deck: The State government replaced the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020, with the new Greater Bengaluru Governance Act, 2024, in 2025, which dissolved the BBMP and formed five corporations in its place, with a pan-city body called the GBA, which came into force on September 2, 2025
briefs.bodyText:
Even as the five new corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) are close to completing a year since they were formed, old problems on the ground continue to haunt citizens, while they now seek a way out of new problems.
The State government replaced the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020, with the new Greater Bengaluru Governance Act, 2024, in 2025, which dissolved the BBMP and formed five corporations in its place, with a pan-city body called the GBA, which came into force on September 2, 2025.
The restructuring was envisaged to address micro-level issues through decentralisation of the administration. While the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) was split into five corporations, what mattered on the ground was that the number of wards in the city almost doubled from 198 to 369, which it was hoped would take the administration closer to citizens.
But this has made little difference on the ground. Even a year later, the city corporations are still mostly working with a workforce deployed for the old 198-ward setup and not upgraded to the 369 wards yet. Moreover, the vacancy rate is around 40%. This essentially means, the intended benefits of the new governance structure is yet to reach citizens.
R. Rajagopalan, convenor of Bengaluru Coalition, puts it this way: the GBA is like a novel concept on paper without an execution plan.
With the change in wards from 198 to 369, citizens struggle to find the engineers in charge of their wards, which forces them to visit corporation offices even for minor inconveniences.
Sneha Nandihal, co-founder, I Change Indiranagar, said there is still confusion about how the new system works. “All our engineers have dual charges, and when we question them about anything, they very conveniently say that they are just in-charge of specific work and get away. The accountability is missing,” she stressed.
Pranith B., a resident of Koramangala, pointed out that in the past, engineers would often visit their wards and ward committee meetings used to take place. “Now, once the complaint is raised, as they don’t visit often, follow-up becomes very hard, and repeated calls won’t yield a response. While many could get their issues resolved by visiting corporation offices, for the working class and labour class, accessing basic amenities has become hard,” he said.
V. Ramprasad, a solid waste management expert, pointed out that addressing the garbage issue needs micro-level planning, which requires a ward-wise blueprint. “At present, such planning has taken a hit with the dearth of engineers. Right from collecting waste to monitoring blackspots, we need sustained efforts, but staff shortage doesn’t allow such focus,” he said.
No space for experimentation
The commissioners, who spoke on condition of anonymity, admitted that the shortage forces them to curtail their ambitious plans and stick to managing everyday crises rather than experimenting with new solutions to existing problems.
“At their disposal, each officer is executing tasks meant for two or three officers. There has been no compromise in managing everyday issues, but existing staff is overwhelmed and there is less scope for collaborative experimentation,” a commissioner said.
For example, an official pointed out the reduction of congestion at the Kaggadasapura Railway Crossing in east Bengaluru following a new traffic model devised by the east city corporation and said, “Such micro-level issues are what was envisioned to be solved through restructuring. But in reality, there are only a few examples like that in the past year to show because the required strength is not available.”
Delay in new rules
The State government has been working on a dedicated Cadre and Recruitment (C&R) Rules for the GBA, but is yet to notify them a year after the authority was formed. Once the new C&R Rules are adopted, it is expected that the government will directly recruit more people for the GBA.
M. Maheshwar Rao, Chief Commissioner of GBA, told The Hindu that new C&R rules have been framed by a committee headed by former Chief Secretary T.M. Vijay Bhaskar and have been sent to the government for approval. “Initially, ground-level requirements were assessed and sent to the government, but we were asked to rework. Then the committee was set up, and recently it gave a report,” Mr. Rao said.
(This is the first of a series of reports evaluating the restructuring of Bengaluru governance, with GBA and five corporations, a year after the reform)

briefs.headline: Healthy eating at school, but junk food outside: Bengaluru schools face a tough challenge
briefs.bodyText:
Although several schools have been putting systems in place to inculcate healthy eating habits among children on the campuses, many principals say that they cannot have control over the choice of food when the schoolchildren step out. As a result, many children anyway end up eating junk or unhealthy snacks, the principals rue.
For instance, some CBSE schools and international schools in the city have installed “sugar board” and “oil board” as per the CBSE norms. They aim to educate children on low consumption of sugar and oil. Some had started this even before the CBSE made it mandatory for all schools to follow.
Oil board, sugar board
Latha M., director, Sandeepani Academy for Excellence, said, “We have a food policy in our school for the last 12 years where we have restrictions on consumption of maida, sugar, deep fried food, factory processed foods like biscuits, sauces, mayonnaise. Even before the CBSE made it mandatory to put up oil board and sugar board to create awareness, it was a norm here. We have also informed parents not to pack these items. Instead, they can pack a fistful of nuts, fresh fruits for short break.”
Ms. Latha added, “However, we receive queries from parents if pooris can be packed. It is definitely a no from us. Similarly, no cakes, chocolates are allowed during birthdays.”
While expressing happiness over the State government’s recent order of banning junk food within 50 metre radius of the school campuses, She said, “It is not possible for schools to have control over students when they step out. There are a few children whose parents send money to buy snacks, cakes from bakeries, food stalls, etc. Once in a while, it is fine but doing it every day is not good for their health.”
Prathima Patil, principal, Ryan International Academy, said, “One of our most cherished initiatives is the daily fruit break. Every morning, each child enjoys a fresh fruit brought from home. It is heartening to see how children now remind each other to bring fruits, and parents share photos of their children excitedly picking out fruits the night before.”
Ms. Prathima highlighted that the sugar board presented in their school corridor is a game changer. “Children learn visually from this board about the actual sugar quantity present in each processed cold drinks and different foods.”
Advice to parents
Ms. Prathima’s advice to parents is children mirror what they see. “If you reach for a fruit when hungry, your child will too. When parents reinforce this at home, we are not just preventing sick days, we are raising a generation of children who make conscious choice for their well being,” she added.
Inventure Academy, another international school in the city, has their own kitchen where chefs and nutritionists discuss and put up a week’s menu, share it with parents.
Ekta Bhasin, who is involved in preparing the menu, said, “At our school, we provide breakfast, mid-morning snack, lunch and evening snack. All these items have equal amount of protein, carbs, vitamins and more. Sugar and Maida are minimal.”
Definitely, we cannot have control over what they eat out of school or at homes. But we make sure to implement best practices of eating at our school, Ms. Bhasin said.
App to help eat better
Ms. Ekta also shared that Grade 11 students of their school have developed a mobile app. “This app can be downloaded and used by anybody to scan the processed food packets. The app provides information on the amount of fats, sugar, carbs, etc. to the kids. It is left to them to eat it or discard.”

stories.headline: ‘We’ll see more Japanese portfolio flows’
stories.deck: Japanese investors are showing strong confidence in India's economic growth potential. Political and policy certainty in India is encouraging more Japanese capital to flow. India's growing economy offers tremendous returns, attracting significant overseas investment. Japanese household money is expected to increase investments in India's market. This trend signifies a positive shift towards…
stories.bodyText:
Nippon Life India Asset Management Company MD & CEO 
Sandeep Sikka
, who was re-elected AMFI president, was part of a 200-member business delegation that accompanied commerce & industry minister Piyush Goyal to Japan last week. In an interview, Sikka argues that there will be a rush of investments from Japan, with FDI translating into higher portfolio flows as retail investors also join. Excerpts:
Mood among Japanese investors...
The relationship between India and Japan is only getting better. We are seeing the conversion of good political relations into good business relations. Both the countries have different strengths: India has scale, talent and growth, while Japan has capital and technology. The conversation has now shifted from why invest in India to how much more to invest. The internal discussion in Japanese boards is moving from assembling in India for the local market to making in India and making for the world.
Concerns over predictable policies, repatriation of profits...
We have been in India for a long time and there are a lot of investors who invest through us. We are owned 75% by Nippon and from our point of view repatriation of dividends has been smooth. 
There is a lot of political and policy certainty in India now. Since Mr Modi became PM, Japan has seen five or six PMs. At the roundtable with foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), the sentiment was very strong.
After FDI, we are going to see more Japanese portfolio flows. Japan has a savings pool of $14 trillion, of which half is in bank accounts. Of the asset management money of $2.2 trillion, one-third, which is around $800 billion, is invested overseas and India gets around 1% of that. Now, more household money will come to India. Through NISA, Japanese govt is trying to encourage more overseas investment and Nippon just launched a scheme for that.
India is world’s fastest growing economy it offers tremendous returns. It always starts with FDI, which is followed by FPI and then retail. We have funds focused on different categories of Japanese investors and there is a very positive trend of AUM and flows of India-focused funds in Japan: from $6.7 billion in 2016 to $9.7 billion in 2021 and $19.6 billion in 2026.
No jitters, Indian MF investors going strong
One or two months do not affect the overall trend. New investors have been coming into the market; new SIPs were opened and gross inflows remained positive. Investors have matured, during times when markets are choppy, they invest lumpsum, otherwise, they prefer SIPs.
Worst of West Asia over
Crude prices have an impact on import bills and current account deficit, which impacts the rupee. The FCNR(B) initiative has been very successful. FPI inflows have turned positive after outflows for a few months, and the rupee seems to have stabilised. So, things are falling in line.
Impact of CAS
It is a step in the right direction as it seeks to build transparency into the system. Any structural change takes time to settle and things will get better. It will help mutual funds in better price discovery, which is good for NAV and reduces tracking error differences in passive funds.

stories.headline: Despite global headwinds, Q1 growth seen resilient on demand, government capex
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Despite facing significant headwinds from late onset of southwest monsoon and geopolitical uncertainties caused by lingering conflict in West Asia and uncertain tariff policies, growth momentum in April-June quarter is likely to have held up — aided by consumer spending, govt capex, robust growth in exports, along with manufacturing and construction sectors.
Economists reckon gross domestic product (GDP) likely grew 7- 7.5% in Q1 FY2026-27, a tad slower than 7.8% in Q4 of 2025-26, though higher than 6.8% recorded in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. In its latest monetary policy review earlier this month, RBI pegged June quarter growth at 7%.
The National Statistical Office (NSO) is scheduled to release official GDP data for Q1 on Monday.
However, economists anticipate a slight moderation in growth during subsequent quarters due to high base effect and the renewed hostilities in the Iran -US conflict, which could affect energy prices and corporate margins .
HDFC Bank principal economist Sakshi Gupta expects Q1 headline print at 7.5% and nominal growth to cross 13%, as manufacturing and electricity propelled industrial growth, while the pass through effect of income tax and GST rate cuts sustained consumer spending on the demand side. “Quarterly earnings results showed the impact on profit margins due to higher input costs has been partly offset by higher volume sales with strong net sales in auto, consumer durables and power,” she added.
DBS Bank senior economist Radhika Rao said high frequency indicators in Q1 suggest that the economy weathered geopolitical disruptions “better” than initially feared and clocked 7.5% growth. “Industrial activity accelerated, although demand for industrial fuels and downstream petroleum products remained soft following price adjustments.” Bank of Baroda chief economist Madan Sabnavis moderates growth expectations to 7% in Q1 as delayed monsoon, lower reservoir levels and aggravated heatwave conditions are likely to pull agricultural growth lower (3.5%) than 4.4% in Q1 of 2025-26. Although, agriculture growth is expected to pick up in the coming quarters.
ICRA Ratings chief economist Aditi Nayar also expects growth to cool down to 7% in Q1 as profit growth of a large group of non-finance companies slowed vis - a vis Q4 FY2025-26, amid sizable losses experienced by oil companies.
“The gross value added in services sector is expected to have slowed down, amid a broad - based deceleration across all sub -sectors,” she added.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu’s business houses line up for the IPO route
stories.deck: Chennai-headquartered drone technology company Garuda Aerospace and a consumer durables company Sathya Agencies are expected to join the IPO queue.
stories.bodyText:
Several relatively newer Tamil Nadu-based business houses are shedding their conservative tag and knocking on SEBI’s doors to tap the IPO market. Two companies Milky Mist, headquartered in Erode, and Chennai-based Lalithaa Jewellery have already gone public this year and witnessed strong subscription. Few more are expected to join the queue in the coming months. Chennai-headquartered drone technology company Garuda Aerospace and a consumer durables company Sathya Agencies are also expected to join the IPO queue.
“Each year, around three to four companies from Tamil Nadu are getting listed,” said an analyst tracking the markets. Over the last three years, several Tamil Nadu-based companies including Avalon Technologies Ltd., R.K. Swamy Ltd., Northern Arc Capital Ltd., Dr. Agarwal’s Healthcare Ltd. and Glottis Ltd., have tapped the IPO market.
“The promoter-driven mindset is slowly changing. People have started realising that if I own 100% of the company, its value may be ₹100, but if I share at least 25% with the public, the company’s value could rise to ₹500. ”That kind of value creation was not known earlier,” said Nagappan Valliappan, a capital market professional who was the former chairman of the Federation of Indian Stock Exchanges.
“If you look at family businesses in Tamil Nadu, many of them are now in their third or fourth generation. There are family disputes and divisions taking place. As a result, some businesses feel it is better to go public and, after a point, sell the company rather than deal with family tussles,” said a source who has been dealing with family businesses in Tamil Nadu.
Pranav Haldea, managing director of Prime Database Group, said: “What you are seeing in Tamil Nadu is what I like to call the ‘net worth creation effect’. This has happened across India over the last 5-6 years. Class B/C towns and cities in India have been largely dominated by family-controlled and closely held businesses which were never too keen on getting outside investors.”
Mr. Haldea added: “What happened was a few IPOs of such type of companies started happening and others saw the kind of valuation and net worth creation which can happen when value is unlocked through an IPO, with several of these promoters becoming millionaires or even billionaires. This triggered a sense of FOMO (fear of missing out) among other family-owned businesses.”
According to data shared by Prime Database, a provider of information on the capital markets, 2023 saw 57 issues across India, raising ₹49,436 crore. In 2024, the number increased to 91 issues, raising ₹1,59,784 crore. The momentum continued in 2025, with 103 issues raising ₹1,75,914 crore. In the current year (2026), the numbers stand at 61 issues, raising ₹72,283 crore.
Those who have gone public through an IPO say that it has made them more disciplined and accountable. You are constantly tracked, and you are answerable to your shareholders. “The capital gives us the ability to invest in the next phase of growth, but equally important is the discipline that comes with being a public company,” K. Rathnam, whole time director and chief executive officer, Milky Mist Dairy Food said.

stories.headline: When age matters
stories.deck: Are you interested in earning a dividend income? Should source of returns matter? The answer is your age determines preference for source of returns, especially via equity investments
stories.bodyText:
In recent times, several stocks have traded at prices that offer good dividend yield. This leads to the question: Are individuals interested in earning a dividend income? Should source of returns matter? Here, we discuss how your age determines your preference for source of returns, especially from equity investments.
Income vs. capital appreciation
Equity investments, like bonds and real estate, offer two sources of returns — income returns and capital appreciation. Income returns arise from dividends received from the firm whose stocks you directly hold. You can also earn dividend income indirectly via net asset value if you invest in mutual funds. Note, this dividend income is reinvested and realised as capital appreciation if you invest in the growth option of a fund.
The choice of returns depends on age. If you are a working executive, your main objective is to accumulate wealth to achieve life goals such as funding child’s education and buying a house.
This tilts your preference towards capital appreciation and is tax efficient; you pay taxes only when you sell a stock in direct investments or when you redeem mutual fund units. Now, goal-based investments are typically held for more than 12 months. So, if you have earmarked these investments for a life goal, the gains are likely to be taxed at 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh in a year. This is because these equity investments will be taxed as long-term capital asset.
What if you are retired? Your active income would have stopped and you now depend on passive income to meet post-retirement expenses.
This means you need monthly income to support lifestyle expenses. Also, most mass-affluent retirees are conservative investors viz. they prefer to conserve capital and consume income. In such cases, they prefer to invest in monthly income bank deposits. Investing in dividend yield stocks may be preferred by some as an additional source of income.
Conclusion
If taxes were the only consideration, then earning dividend income may not be an economical source of returns.
This is because dividend income is taxed at your marginal tax rate. Yet, retirees may prefer dividend as a supplement to their interest income to meet their post-retirement expenses.
In such cases, think of taxes as the cost retirees are willing to incur to consume income without drawing down their investment capital — selling shares or mutual fund units to generate cash flows.
(The author offers training programs for individuals to manage their personal investments)

briefs.headline: SBI and SBI Capital Markets to dilute up to 1% stake in NSE offer
CEO’s exit to end uncertainty at HDFC
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Sashidhar Jagdishan’s decision to step down as HDFC Bank’s MD & CEO is set to remove a layer of uncertainty around the leadership of the country’s second-largest bank, giving the board and the incoming chief executive a clear runway to execute an ambitious plan to build a bank of global scale.
Jagdishan will retire from the bank on Oct 26 after deciding not to seek reappointment. The decision comes at a point when HDFC Bank is emerging from one of the most consequential periods in its history, having completed its merger with HDFC and begun recalibrating its business and growth strategy for the post-merger phase.
His departure allows the board to make a clean leadership transition without the possibility of an unresolved succession question continuing to hang over the institution. The new chief executive, whether chosen from within the bank or brought in from outside, will inherit a platform that has already undergone the disruption and integration associated with the merger and can focus on execution rather than managing a prolonged transition. Kaizad Bharucha, deputy MD, who has been on the board for 12 years, is seen as an internal frontrunner.
Over the last few weeks, several issues have been resolved: from the appointment of a new chairman in Rajeev Kumar to acting against the problems with “mis-selling” in Dubai, as well as penalties on executives, including Jagdishan, in the Maharashtra PSU case, where irregularities in raising deposits were brought to the fore.
The timing is particularly important because HDFC Bank is now a substantially larger and more systemically important institution. With a balance sheet of about half a trillion dollars and around 100 million customers, the bank has become an increasingly important part of the Indian financial system. Its scale also means that scrutiny of its operations, governance and performance is unlikely to diminish.
The challenge for the incoming chief, therefore, will be more about converting its scale into sustained growth and improving performance. The bank has a large distribution network, a massive customer base and a technology architecture that provides the foundation for the next phase of expansion.
The post-merger recalibration had also created a period in which growth, margins and the business mix came under greater scrutiny. As the effects of the merger and the associated base effects fade, the focus is likely to shift towards how effectively the bank can use its distribution advantage, technology investments and changing business mix to accelerate growth and improve returns.
This gives the succession process an unusual character. The incoming CEO does not necessarily need to rebuild the bank or undertake another fundamental transformation. The task is to run the existing platform more effectively, sharpen execution and pursue the board’s larger ambition of making HDFC Bank one of the world’s top banks.
According to board-level sources, the bank has considerable management depth to draw upon, leaving open the possibility of an internal candidate taking over or the appointment of an external executive who can bring a fresh perspective. Either route would benefit from the clarity created by Jagdishan’s decision not to seek another term.
For investors, the transition could therefore mark the end of one chapter rather than the beginning of another period of uncertainty. Jagdishan’s tenure was dominated by the challenge of integrating HDFC Ltd with HDFC Bank, while the next phase is likely to be judged increasingly on growth, profitability, technology and the ability to translate the combined institution’s scale into a globally competitive banking franchise.

briefs.headline: From sweet to sour crude: India’s bitumen supply improves, but prices remain elevated
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India had faced a severe bitumen shortage at the peak of the West Asia crisis despite receiving crude supplies from Russia. The reason was that Russian oil is predominantly “sweet crude”, making it unsuitable for producing high-quality bitumen. Availability of bitumen has improved now with higher domestic production and increased imports of Venezuelan crude. However, Venezuelan crude, which yields more bitumen, comes with its own challenge — it is “sour crude” with higher sulphur content and is costlier to process.
Officials said that while availability is no longer a major concern, bitumen costs remain significantly higher than in the pre-war period. Data show that the price of VG-40 bitumen, the grade most widely used for road and highway projects in India, spiked from Rs 52,000-55,000 per tonne before the conflict to over Rs 1 lakh per tonne in May, after crude supplies from West Asia were severely disrupted due to the closure of Strait of Hormuz.
Since then, there has been a moderation in prices, though not enough to bring relief to road-owning agencies and road builders. 
As per latest data, the price of VG-40 bitumen as of Aug 16 was in the range of Rs 85,000 to Rs 86,000 per tonne. Industry insiders and officials said they are hopeful of further correction in prices, but there is no possibility of the prices going back to pre-war levels.
“This means the elevated cost of bitumen is expected to keep road construction and highway project costs at a higher level. Govt will have to continue providing compensation for ongoing projects and revise the cost of projects that it plans to bid out,” said an industry expert who didn’t wish to be named.
Going by industry reports, bitumen prices range from Rs 66,000 to Rs 86,000 per tonne depending on the grade, depot location and whether it is supplied in bulk or packed drums. “As of now, we have no availability issue as the pace of laying of bituminous layers is less during the rainy season. We will have to wait for the Oct-Feb period, which are crucial months for achieving the road construction target. Demand during that period will be more,” said a senior executive of a highway developer.

briefs.headline: Bullion watch: What will shape gold, silver prices? Fed bets, US jobs data in focus
briefs.deck: Throughout September, gold and silver prices are likely to remain under pressure. Critical influences on trading will stem from forthcoming US employment data releases. Traders should be alert to how central bank anticipations and persistent geopolitical tensions will steer market dynamics. Special attention will be given to non-farm payrolls and unemployment rates, as market players speculate on…
briefs.bodyText:
Gold and silver prices could remain under pressure in September, with US employment data, central-bank expectations and geopolitical tensions likely to drive trading.
The bullion market is set to enter the month on a cautious note the after witnessing a sharp sell-off last week. On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), gold futures for October delivery lost Rs 6,157, or 3.8 per cent, to end the week at Rs 1.56 lakh per 10 grams. Silver futures for September delivery fell Rs 9,893, or 4 per cent, to Rs 2.36 lakh per kilogram.
"MCX Gold witnessed a sharp correction last week, falling from around Rs 1.63 lakh to Rs 1.56 lakh per 10 grams, resulting in a decline of nearly over Rs 6,000 from the weekly peak and a negative weekly closing of more than 3 per cent," Jateen Trivedi, VP research analyst - commodity and currency, LKP Securities told PTI.
The decline was also visible in overseas markets. Comex gold futures for December delivery fell $150.7, or 3.2 per cent, over the week to settle at $4,680.6 per ounce. Silver futures declined $2.56, or 3.64 per cent, to $67.78 per ounce.
According to Pranav Mer, senior vice president, EBG - commodity & currency research, JM Financial Services Ltd, selling intensified on Friday following Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's speech. 
The Fed chief's commentary on inflation and monetary policy led to profit booking across bullion markets, Mer said.
Geopolitical tensions add to market uncertainty
Geopolitical developments will remain another key focus. Traders will continue to monitor the US-Iran conflict, while developments around the Strait of Hormuz could influence oil prices and inflation expectations.
Despite the steep weekly decline, silver maintained a stronger monthly performance than gold in August. Silver gained around 21 per cent during the month, compared with a 15.7 per cent rise in the yellow metal, Gaurav Garg, head of Research at Lemonn markets desk, said.
Trivedi said, "The combination of dollar movement, labour-market data, Fed expectations and geopolitical headlines is likely to determine whether gold stabilises after the recent correction or enters another phase of profit booking."
US jobs data, Fed policy bets in focus
The spotlight now shifts to US labour-market indicators, with traders watching non-farm payrolls, unemployment data and ADP non-farm employment change. The readings could influence expectations around Federal Reserve policy ahead of its September meeting, Mer said.
"The coming week is likely to remain highly volatile, with market participants attempting to price in the probability of a September Federal Reserve policy change," Trivedi said.
Markets will also assess manufacturing and services PMI data from major economies, including India. Inflation figures from the Eurozone and Germany, along with US non-farm payroll data due towards the end of the week, will be closely tracked.

briefs.headline: FPIs continue to buy: Foreign investors pump over Rs 30,900 crore into Indian equities in August
briefs.deck: In August, foreign investors poured Rs 30,919 crore into Indian equity markets, signaling a notable turnaround following earlier withdrawals. Investor confidence strengthened due to rising corporate earnings and a stable rupee. Additionally, diminishing geopolitical worries positively influenced emerging market investments. Nevertheless, ongoing risks related to Middle Eastern tensions and…
briefs.bodyText:
Foreign investors returned to Indian equities in August with a stronger buying pace, putting Rs 30,919 crore into the market and extending their net purchases for the second month. The latest inflow came after Rs 20,200 crore was invested in July, offering a marked change from the aggressive selling through the first half of the year.
FPIs had withdrawn Rs 49,340 crore in June, Rs 32,963 crore in May, Rs 60,847 crore in April and Rs 1.17 lakh crore in March. Before that, foreign investors had put Rs 22,615 crore into Indian equities in February, according to CDSL data.
The two consecutive months of inflows have come after what was the worst six-month stretch in years and could be an early sign that foreign investor flows are beginning to change direction. Yet, the overall picture for 2026 remains negative, with FPIs having taken out Rs 2.23 lakh crore from Indian equities so far. The figure has already surpassed the Rs 1.66 lakh crore withdrawn during the whole of 2025.
"The important factors driving the FPI flows into India are the reversal of the chip trade, the stability in the rupee and, more importantly, the improving earnings growth in India," V K Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist, Geojit Investments, said.
Improvement in corporate performance during the June quarter helped strengthen investor confidence, alongside continued economic activity and higher credit growth.
"Corporate earnings showed signs of improvement during the June quarter, helping ease concerns around the earnings slowdown that had weighed on foreign investor sentiment earlier. Resilient economic activity and strengthening credit growth also reinforced confidence in India's medium- to long-term growth prospects," Himanshu Srivastava, principal, manager research, Morningstar Investment Research India, said.
The global backdrop was also more supportive at times during August. A reduction in geopolitical concerns improved risk appetite, while expectations of lower US interest rates supported the case for emerging-market allocations. The rotation of global money away from the heavily crowded AI and semiconductor trade in Korea and Taiwan also created scope for additional investment in India, Srivastava added.
Foreign flows still faced risks, with Middle East tensions and uncertainty over crude oil prices weighing down sentiment.
"Cash flows suggest returning conviction; futures suggest lingering caution. The trend may be turning, post AI and war-related worries receding," Manish Bhandari, CEO and portfolio manager, Vallum Capital, said.
The direction of crude oil prices and developments in US-Iran tensions will be among the key factors watched by investors in the coming period. Any escalation in US-Canada trade tensions could increase uncertainty in financial markets and prompt investors to remain cautious, Pabitro Mukherjee, Deputy Vice President-Research, Bajaj Broking, said.
US bond yields are another concern. Investors are also awaiting inflation data before the Federal Reserve's policy meeting in mid-September.
For India, Q1 GDP growth and inflation readings will be important indicators for institutional flows, Mukherjee added.
Foreign investors also made selective investments in the debt market during the month. They put Rs 627 crore through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) and another Rs 289 crore through the Voluntary Retention Route (VRR). At the same time, they withdrew Rs 2,318 crore through the general route.
